caption:
Queen Victoria switched on Glasgow's tap water 💧
On 14 October 1859 she opened a sluice at Loch Katrine, and the water ran to the city by gravity through nearly 26 miles of aqueduct, 13 miles of it hard-rock tunnel. Over 3,000 people built it. Today Scottish Water says the aqueduct feeds the Milngavie and Balmore treatment works and supplies more than 1.3 million people.
